dedupe_keys.name: eat lancet 2025 food system data country level food consumption production and environmental impacts under benchmark and flexitarian diets 2010 2050

description: This workbook holds the food system numbers behind the 2025 EAT-Lancet Commission: how much food each country would consume and produce, and with what environmental impact, under current trends compared with a healthy flexitarian diet. The producer is Marco Springmann of University College London, who ran the analysis for the Commission's report in The Lancet. Coverage is global with country-level detail for 2010, 2020, 2030, 2040 and 2050, giving food consumption and production and food-related environmental impacts measured against planetary boundaries. The results come from DIA-GIO, a biophysical input-output model linking diets, production and trade, whose method was published in Nature in 2018. The workbook is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: scenario outputs, not observations, a large workbook with limited documentation in the record, and results depend on the model's diet and trade assumptions. Simulation uses: setting future national food demand and production mixes for food supply and logistics models, and testing the infrastructure implications of dietary shifts. Related records: the global food security projections database (data-global-food-security-projections-database) compares other demand projections, and FAOSTAT food balances (data-faostat) give the baseline supply.
